ingredients.item: hairtail , cut into 10 cm fingers, or whole if your grill is long enough
toasted sesame seeds , sliced scallion , lemon wedge or splash of vinegar
Steamed rice , kimchi , and a light soy-vinegar dip

instructions.heading: Step 1
instructions.action: Fingers skin-down on the oiled moderate grate, 3–4 minutes undisturbed. The skin will tighten, silver going pewter, then blister gold at the edges.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the skin lifts clean where it crisped and stays put where it has not — work from the done end with the spatula, not all at once. The flesh at the cut ends turns opaque upward from the skin.

instructions.heading: Step 2
instructions.action: One gentle flip, 2–3 minutes more, off the fire when the flesh at the thickest finger's center is opaque and flakes at a fork's nudge.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: a test finger pulled apart: opaque through, sweet and firm-juicy, the spine releasing from the meat with no resistance. Hairtail's flesh is dense but delicate — it will not forgive much past this point, but it does not need to; the clock is short.

instructions.heading: Step 3
instructions.action: Platter, sesame and scallion over, lemon beside, and the eating is handwork: lift the spine free of each finger, the meat in one or two pieces.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: eating test: crisp skin and sweet white meat in the same bite, the soy-vinegar dip for the pieces that want brightening. If the skin is leathery instead of crisp, the finger went on wet — the drying law is the record.

storageNotes: Salted fingers hold 24 hours refrigerated. Cooked, 2 days — the meat lifts off the spine in clean strips for rice bowls or gimbap filling.

Variations: a light dusting of flour before the grill (the Busan street style) for a crisper coat at the cost of some skin's shine; the same cure on mackerel (#SF07) at a longer clock; the gochujang swipe at the end for the spicy table.
